patterns.property: abandoned first plan / original request stated as happening or holding is never the key
patterns.evidence: Every Part 1 script is request -> obstacle -> fallback, and the setting-obvious original plan is always a distractor: 'Sit outside on the balcony to watch the boats' (E-D1), 'Run laps on the outdoor track' (D-D2), 'Send the woman a text once the wallet is found' (F-D2), 'Hang it above the sofa today' (G-D4), 'Begin filming at tomorrow's practice' (H-C-4). Only exception-like case E-D2 asks what she ASKED, not what happens.

patterns.property: intent-next key = the workaround offered after the obstacle, or the last commitment spoken
patterns.evidence: 13/13. Keys read as qualified substitutes: 'Take a table inside that still looks over the river', 'Use an exercise machine', 'Make a label for the instrument', 'Fill in the guitar part on a piano', 'Copy two of the pictures with a library machine'.

patterns.property: key is one of the closest-worded twin pair (convergence)
patterns.evidence: Items with a unique most-similar pair (word Jaccard >= 0.30): key inside it 17/20 (chance 10/20); part 3 13/15, main-idea 5/5, attitude 3/3. 'How a firewood price limit harmed the poor' / '...kept poor homes warm' (F-L-6); 'It was a worthy aim, served by the wrong method' / '...served well by the rule' (F-L-4); 'larger than' / 'smaller than' (B-L-6). Misses: G-C-4, G-L-1, I-L-3.

patterns.property: key is OUTSIDE the closest-worded twin pair (reverse convergence)
patterns.evidence: Part 1 twins are distractor pairs 7/9: 'Pack six of the duck eggs' / 'Pack six of the hen eggs' (key: four duck), 'Fitting a rack would cost too much money' / '...take too long today', 'He has to take it to the shop himself tonight.' / 'He has to print it in the library tomorrow.' Opposite direction from parts 2-3, so a student who learns both rules gains on both.

patterns.property: part 2 conversations: the woman's side prevails; options where the man's counter-plan or refusal wins are never key
patterns.evidence: All 9 Part 2 scripts end with W's plan adopted, conditionally adopted or put to a vote she proposed. Never key: 'Being persuaded to keep the bird migration poster', 'How the man persuades the student to use the window ledge', 'A coach refuses a student's request...', 'Why the woman should give up rowing until the test', 'Agreeing to sell their dad's old drum kit'.

patterns.property: main-idea twin resolved toward the conditional / deferred / compromise outcome over a flat one
patterns.evidence: '...which they will decide later' over '...which the man agrees to at last'; '...that the club will vote on' over '...and choosing the letter'; 'lend' over 'give away for good'; 'gets the coach to agree' (with conditions) over refuses/persuades.

patterns.property: main-idea key is the broadest option when scopes differ; narrow moment-details and general-world topics never key
patterns.evidence: 9/9 where options differ in scope (the other 8 main-ideas use parallel frames, covered by the twin pattern). 'How a way of estimating animal numbers works, and its limits' vs 'How heavy rain can wear the paint dots off...'; world-topic distractors 'How green wood differs from dry, seasoned wood', 'Why fungus grows on the floors of damp caves', 'How blood moves from the heart around the body' never key.

patterns.property: attitude key is the favourable / approving option
patterns.evidence: Uniquely favourable in 5 (D-L-4 'Confident that the order is right' vs Doubtful/Unsure/Unsure; G-L-4 'It is better than expected'; H-C-3; I-C-1 'They're better than any the man made.'; I-L-6 'It still surprises the speaker.' vs three dismissals), one of two favourable in C-L-6 and F-L-4. Only B-L-4 keys a critical view.

patterns.property: attitude key is never the longest option
patterns.evidence: 0/8 strictly longest (chance 2/8). Batch-wide length is balanced (27/126), so this is kind-local.

patterns.property: attitude key is a comparative ('than expected', 'more than', 'easier than')
patterns.evidence: 'It makes the work look easier than it is', 'It deserves more praise than a sudden idea would.', 'It is better than expected', 'They're better than any the man made.'

patterns.property: inference key repeats the fewest prompt words
patterns.evidence: Key at the minimum (ties included) 7/8; key strictly echoes most 0/8. Single-word echoes: D-L-5 'single wave hitting a crack' -> distractors 'reaches a crack only once a day', 'makes the crack close up'. Batch-wide 27/39 (69%), under the bar. Weak: overlaps are 0-2 words.

patterns.property: numeric scale of four values: key is the second-largest, never an extreme
patterns.evidence: one night / 2-3 days / ~7 days* / a month; 150 / 200 / 300* / 400; 20 / 50 / 100* / 300 years. n=3, minimum size.

patterns.property: part 1 purpose key gives the reason for the speaker's request/choice; 'To ask ...' never key
patterns.evidence: 'To explain why twelve rolls are needed', 'To explain the choice to stay on the bus', 'To argue the voice is warmed up', 'To show the cheaper service will be in time'; C-D1 is the exception. 'To ask ...' options 0/4 across A-D1, I-D2, I-D3.

patterns.property: regex-level author/kind tics at small n
patterns.scope: author C, author F, author I, kind attitude, kind main-idea, kind inference, kind purpose, author E
patterns.evidence: Author C key 'X more than Y' frame 3/4 ('cares more about the plants than an early arrival', 'thought about the eggs more than about keeping the hens safe'); author F comparative 6/8; hedge: author C 3/4, author I 0/3, attitude 0/3; negative: author C 3/4, attitude 0/3, main-idea 0/3; contrast word: inference 0/4; comma: inference 0/3; number: author E 4/5, purpose 3/4; unique first word: author F 0/3. All n=3-8, keyword regex; treat as weak.

checked_clean: key strictly longest: 27/126 (each author 3/14; part 3 9/54) - balanced
key has most transcript content words (ratio): 57/126; fewest: 35/126
key repeats most prompt words: 10/39; fewest 27/39 (69%, below bar batch-wide)
key has a first word no other option shares: 13/34
key is the most 'central' option (highest summed similarity to the others): 27/99
purpose frame verbs: explain 3/19, show 4/16, suggest 1/8, say 2/6, warn 1/4 - mixed
Part 1 relationship keys: 5 items, all plain role pairs vs plausible role pairs; no wording tell
lecture key always the speaker's stated view: true by construction, but the nuanced/'cannot tell yet' option is mixed (key in F-L-4, C-C-3; distractor in A-L-4, G-L-2 'only possible cause')
tone-built distractors (careless/rude, e.g. A-C-4 'sport matters more than the test', A-C-2 'preparing alone'): too few (<3 clear) to count
near-identical key wording across scripts: none found beyond the purpose 'to explain why/the choice' frame (A-D1, I-D2)
